text:
marta: Quick heads-up — canary perf traces from yesterday show a ton of [unknown] frames in the CUDA kernel timeline. NVTX ranges are present (labels show up) but there are no source file:line annotations for libredwood_runtime.so and some aten kernels. I uploaded the .nsys: s3://redwood-traces/serving_canary_1918765432.nsight

kai: Can you paste the nsys command you used to capture it? Also which container image?

marta: Ran locally against the canary image:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt -o serving_canary_1918765432 \
  /opt/redwood/bin/serve --config /etc/redwood/canary.yaml
```
Image: registry.redwood/internal/serving:2026-04-05-canary

kai: Two usual suspects: 1) container missing libcupti.so (nsys relies on CUPTI for symbol mapping), 2) debug symbols stripped from the binary / separate debug-info not available to the profiler.

ryan: Confirming — our CI has a post-build step that runs `strip --strip-unneeded` on the runtime artifacts for the release image. Snippet from buildkite:
```
- run: |
  if [ "$BUILDTYPE" = "release" ]; then
    strip --strip-debug out/lib/libredwood_runtime.so || true
  fi
```
That would drop DWARF needed for line info.

olga: Also check CUPTI ABI mismatch: if the host driver/CUDA version doesn't match the libcupti bundled in the container, nsys can still attach but won't always resolve lines. Run inside the container: `ldd /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64/libcupti.so` and compare to host `nvidia-smi` driver version.

marta: Good call. I checked the image: /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI is empty in the container (we baked a slim cuda runtime). We do mount host driver via nvidia-container-runtime but not CUPTI.

kai: Quick repro I did: launched the same image but bind-mounted host CUPTI libs into the container: `-v /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64:/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64:ro` then re-ran nsys. The previously unknown frames resolved to function names and a handful of source:line entries reappeared. So it's definitely missing CUPTI in the image.

marta: Nice repro — that explains the randomness across test infra (some hosts have CUPTI in same path, others don't).

ryan: For the strip issue we should avoid stripping debug symbols in our CI for images we intend to profile. Options: (A) keep full symbols in the debug image and keep release image stripped for size, but upload a separate debug-info bundle to S3 (and document mapping), (B) keep unstripped artifacts in a debug tag (e.g., :canary-debug). I'm leaning to (B) plus automated debug-info uploads.

olga: We'll also need to document a build-id/pathmap approach for perfetto/perf: if debug info is separated, profilers look up build-ids. Add a step in our artifacts upload: `eu-strip --only-keep-debug` + `objcopy --add-gnu-debuglink` and push debug tarball to s3://redwood-debug-symbols/<buildid>. This keeps release image small while preserving debug info elsewhere.

marta: Good list of actions. Immediate next steps I can take: 1) add CUPTI bind-mount to our local dev runbook so engineers can repro easily, 2) open a PR to include CUPTI in diagnostic image (serving:diag) or make it mountable by default, 3) ask infra to make debug artifacts available for the canary tag.

ryan: I'll open the BK PR to stop stripping on the debug pipeline and add an upload step. PR description will include exact objcopy commands.

kai: For capture best-practices note in runbook: run nsys from host with container running and mount both /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI and /usr/lib64/libcudart.so.* if necessary. Example capture command we should standardize:
```
docker run --gpus all --rm -v /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64:/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64:ro \
  -v /tmp/nsys:/tmp/nsys registry.redwood/serving:diag \
  bash -lc "nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt -o /tmp/nsys/serving_canary $(which serve) --config /etc/redwood/canary.yaml"
```

olga: Also add a note about CUPTI versions — prefer shipping the host-matching CUPTI to the diag image rather than relying on containers that may have older CUDA runtimes. That avoids silent failures.

deploy-bot: canary deployment succeeded for serving:2026-04-05-canary at 2026-04-05T14:23:10Z :white_check_mark:

marta: I'll collect the trace + repro notes and put them in an eng-runtime confluence page, then link the PRs. Thanks for the quick debug everyone :rocket:

kai: TL;DR: missing libcupti in the runtime/diagnostic image caused inconsistent symbol/line resolution in nsys; also avoid stripping debug info for debug/canary artifacts and upload separate debug bundles so profilers can map build-id -> DWARF.

ryan: Filing follow-ups: BK PR for debug upload, image PR for diag that includes CUPTI, and runbook update. I'll ping when PRs are up. :thumbsup:
